text:
marta: Heads-up — I'm proposing a new "scoped rollout contract" concept to bind runtime config changes to quota envelopes + telemetry gates. Want feedback before I write the RFC.

kyle: quick tl;dr?

marta: idea is to avoid broad flag flips. A contract includes: scope (service/route/model), quota budget (tokens/reqs), telemetry gates (error/latency delta thresholds), and dry-run profile. Console + API would surface it.

srinivas: I like the safety-first vibe. How would quota budgets interact with existing route quotas? override or lease?

marta: good Q. Plan: contracts request a temporary "lease" against a pool. Controller enforces soft cap, then backoff -> automatic rollback if telemetry gate trips. We don't mutate global quotas unless the lease is committed.

eva: can we see an example API shape?

marta: sketch:

```json
{
  "contract_id": "tmp-2026-04-01-01",
  "scope": {"service": "inference", "route": "/v1/generate", "model": "rw-large-v1"},
  "budget": {"tokens": 2000000, "requests": 20000},
  "telemetry_gate": {"latency_p90_delta_ms": 50, "error_rate_delta_pct": 0.5},
  "dry_run": true,
  "owner": "marta"
}
```

kyle: that looks reasonable. What about partial waves? e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%

marta: contract will accept a waves array with cohorts so leases can be scheduled. Each wave can specify cohort selector (by account, region, tag) and a budget multiplier.

srinivas: sounds close to feature flags + circuit breaker. We need to be explicit about state transitions: REQUESTED -> LEASED -> ACTIVE -> PAUSED -> COMMITTED -> ROLLED_BACK. Also a TTL on LEASED.

eva: console UX thoughts: preview the projected token spend per wave, show historic baseline for telemetry comparisons, and a one-click abort that triggers immediate rollback and marks the contract as ROLLBACK_TRIGGERED.

marta: agreed. Also add an auditor view with the exact diff of config keys the contract will change.

kyle: operationally, who pays if the lease is exceeded during a wave? The customer or internal safety pool?

srinivas: propose a safety pool owned by infra for experiments < X tokens. For customer-initiated > X, require billing approval. That avoids accidental cost explosions.

eva: telemetry gating: do we use absolute thresholds or relative change vs baseline window? I prefer percentage change with a minimum effect size to avoid noise.

marta: plan: relative change vs a rolling 7d baseline plus an absolute floor. e.g. error_rate_delta_pct > 0.5 AND error_count_delta >= 10.

ops-oncall: important: when a gate trips, we MUST emit high-signal alerts (pager) for SEV2 if it affects core routes. Also show the exact commit that triggered it.

marta: noted. We'll add an "alert_profile" field on the contract to map to pager rules.

kyle: implementation notes: controller needs to be idempotent and reconcile state on restart. Also expose a read-only config diff API for the console to render before apply.

srinivas: thinking about race conditions: two contracts might try to lease overlapping quotas for same route. Controller should use a compare-and-reserve with optimistic locking and expose a reason (conflict) to the API.

eva: can we reuse existing flag rollout UI components? probably, but we need to show budget curves and telemetry gates inline.

marta: next steps: I'll draft RFC with schema, state machine, console mocks, and a minimal controller POC. Can folks comment on the schema defaults and safety pool thresholds?

kyle: +1 for RFC. For thresholds, suggest infra pool default 100k tokens / 1k reqs. Anything above requires billing tag.

srinivas: +1. Also add a dry-run mode where payloads are shadowed to the new config and metrics are collected without serving real responses (if feasible).

marta: good call on shadowing. We'll mark it optional per-model (some models can't be shadowed because cost).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: config-controller/experiment-lease-v1 -> staging at 1758881350

marta: thanks @deploy-bot — I'll link the staging POC in the RFC.

ops-oncall: one more: add an SLA override guard. Contracts cannot lower SLAs for a route without a separate approval step.

marta: yep — will include an approval workflow for any change that reduces an SLA or increases cost > billing_threshold.

kyle: spelling nit: rename "telemetry_gate" to "observability_gate"? feels broader.

marta: hmm yeah "observability_gate" is clearer. I'll use that in the RFC.

srinivas: cool. If no objections, I'll help with controller locking design tomorrow.

eva: I'll prototype the console mock Wednesday.

marta: awesome — thanks all. I'll drop a short RFC link here when ready.
